title: The Mind's Canvas
coreMove: Treat the face as a managed display that becomes useful only when timing and the rest of the body give it weight.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar frames the face as expressive but socially managed. The chapter can use smiles, lips, eyebrows, eyelids, jaw tension, gaze limits, timing, mismatch, and whole-body context, but must avoid micro-expression certainty and eye-contact honesty myths.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version makes the face the secret screen of emotion. The writer must show that facial signals matter most when their timing, strain, or mismatch connects with the rest of the body.

hook: Eye contact proves honesty or avoidance proves deception.
A fake smile exposes a hidden feeling by itself.
counterintuition: Most people think faces are unreliable, but actually tiny expressions reveal everything.
The eyes are windows to the soul.
A smile means comfort unless it is fake.
tryThisNow: Set a timer for ninety seconds and read faces.
Watch someone's eyes to see if they are honest.
Practice spotting fake smiles in strangers.

exampleSpecs.domain: pediatric hearing-test booth with a parent watching through glass
exampleSpecs.audience: an audiologist deciding whether a parent understands the next test step
exampleSpecs.stakes: a parent's managed smile can hide confusion that affects consent and cooperation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The parent smiles at the child through the booth glass, but the smile arrives late, the eyelids stay tight, and one hand keeps rereading the test card, so the audiologist pauses to explain the next tone series.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A child-sized headset hangs inside a quiet test booth.
mustAvoid: diagnosing fear from the face alone

exampleSpecs.domain: antique book fair dealer evaluating a restored first edition
exampleSpecs.audience: a dealer weighing a seller's reaction without accusing anyone
exampleSpecs.stakes: a valuable sale needs verification of restoration history, not a facial verdict
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: When the hinge repair is mentioned, the seller's eyebrows lift before the polite smile, her jaw sets while the receipt folder stays closed, and the dealer writes verify repair invoice instead of deciding she is hiding something.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A marbled endpaper opens beside a folded repair receipt.

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant allergy conversation at a chef's counter
exampleSpecs.audience: a server watching whether a guest's smile is social cover for concern
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed concern could create a safety risk, while an accusation would embarrass the guest
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The guest smiles and says any sauce is fine, but the lips press flat after sesame is named, gaze drops to the allergy card, and the shoulders stay still, so the server asks the chef to confirm ingredients aloud.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A laminated allergy card lies beside a small dish of sauce.

exampleSpecs.domain: architect presenting a ramp redesign to a disability advisory board
exampleSpecs.audience: an architect noticing strain before the board formalizes objections
exampleSpecs.stakes: the design can improve if the architect reads mismatch as invitation to ask, not as rejection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two board members nod politely, but one jaw tightens as the slope diagram appears and the nod stops exactly when the landing width is named; the architect asks for the concern before defending the drawing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A ramp slope diagram fills a portable projector screen.

exampleSpecs.domain: family-owned bakery filming a local news segment after a health inspection
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer helping a nervous owner speak plainly on camera
exampleSpecs.stakes: the owner needs to communicate without letting a managed broadcast smile erase visible strain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before the camera rolls, the owner's smile drops whenever the inspection grade is named and her eyelids narrow toward the posted notice; after the producer rehearses the first sentence, the smile arrives with her torso turning back toward the ovens.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A posted inspection notice is taped beside trays of cooling rolls.

exampleSpecs.domain: university lab safety review after a chemical spill report
exampleSpecs.audience: a lab manager listening to a graduate assistant describe what happened
exampleSpecs.stakes: the report needs better reconstruction, but facial tension cannot become an accusation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: In the timeline review, the assistant keeps steady eye contact, but his lips thin and jaw locks only at the waste-container step while his hands flatten the incident form, so the manager marks that step for verification.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A yellow incident form sits beside a labeled waste container.

skillTargets: read smiles, eyelids, lips, jaw tension, gaze, timing, and mismatch as bounded facial evidence
combine facial timing with body, object, or topic context before interpreting
reject eye-contact honesty myths, micro-expression certainty, and face-only verdicts
choose a next move that verifies or clarifies without naming a hidden emotion

tryThisNowSpec: Watch one polite facial expression today and write what happened before it, whether it arrived on time or late, and what the rest of the body or hands did at the same moment.
